unit: Unit 5: Breach of Contract and its Remedies
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Anticipatory Breach of Contract
explain: Breach of contract means failure by a party to perform their contractual obligation.
Anticipatory breach occurs when the promisor refuses or disables performance before the due date arrives.
It can happen expressly through words or impliedly through conduct.
Under Section 39, the promisee may end the contract unless acquiescence is shown by words or conduct.
The aggrieved party can rescind immediately and sue for damages without waiting for the due date.
Alternatively, the promisee can keep the contract alive until the due date, benefiting both parties.

flow.title: Promisee Options in Anticipatory Breach
steps: Promisor refuses performance before due date
Promisee gets two legal options
Option 1: Rescind contract and sue immediately
Option 2: Keep contract alive till due date
Guilty party may still perform if alive
Supervening impossibility may discharge contract

topics.example: A agrees on 15th July to supply cotton to B on 14th August, but informs B on 30th July that he cannot supply.
remember: Section 39 allows the promisee to rescind immediately or wait until the performance date.
mistakes: Assuming anticipatory breach automatically terminates the contract without the promisee's choice.

quiz.q: When a promisor refuses to perform before the due date, it is known as:
quiz.why: Refusal before the performance date arrives is an anticipatory breach under Section 39.

quiz.q: If the promisee elects to keep the contract alive after an anticipatory breach, who benefits?
quiz.why: Keeping the contract alive allows the guilty party to perform or take advantage of supervening impossibility.

topics.title: Actual Breach of Contract
explain: Actual breach occurs when a party refuses or fails to perform on the scheduled date or during performance.
Refusal at the time performance is due gives the other party an immediate right of legal action.
Refusal during performance happens when one party stops fulfilling obligations mid-way.
Unlike anticipatory breach, actual breach occurs on or after the performance date.

flow.title: How Actual Breach Occurs
steps: Contract performance date arrives or performance begins
Party refuses or fails to perform obligation
Actual breach of contract takes place
Aggrieved party gets immediate right to remedies

topics.example: A agrees to deliver 100 bags of sugar to B on 1st February, but fails to deliver them on that day.
remember: Actual breach happens either when performance becomes due or during actual performance.
mistakes: Confusing actual breach occurring during performance with an anticipatory breach prior to the due date.

quiz.q: Actual breach of contract occurs when a party fails to perform:
o: At due date or during performance
quiz.why: Actual breach takes place when performance is due or while performance is underway.

quiz.q: A agrees to deliver sugar on 1st Feb but fails to supply on 1st Feb. This is an example of:
quiz.why: Failure to perform on the scheduled due date constitutes an actual breach.

topics.title: Suit for Damages and Kinds of Damages
explain: Section 73 provides compensation for loss naturally arising in the usual course of events.
Special damages are recoverable only if special circumstances were communicated at the time of contract formation.
No compensation is payable for remote or indirect losses (Hadley v. Baxendale rule).
Exemplary damages apply in breach of promise to marry or wrongful cheque dishonour by a banker.
Nominal damages are small amounts awarded when a breach occurs without actual financial loss.
Deterioration caused by delay can be recovered from a carrier even without prior notice.

flow.title: Assessment of Damages under Section 73
steps: Contract is broken by a party
Identify naturally arising loss from breach
Check if special notice was given initially
Exclude remote or indirect losses completely
Aggrieved party must mitigate the loss
Award reasonable compensation to plaintiff

topics.example: A sells rice to B at Rs 5,000/bag; price rises to Rs 5,500 on delivery day; A refuses delivery, so B claims Rs 500/bag as ordinary damages.
remember: Section 73 explicitly bars compensation for remote and indirect losses.
mistakes: Claiming special damages without proving notice of special circumstances at contract formation.

quiz.q: Under Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act, compensation cannot be claimed for:
quiz.why: Section 73 specifically rules out compensation for remote and indirect losses.

quiz.q: Exemplary or vindictive damages may be awarded for:
o: Wrongful dishonour of cheque by banker
quiz.why: Exemplary damages apply to wrongful cheque dishonour by bankers and breach of promise to marry.

topics.title: Penalty and Liquidated Damages
explain: Liquidated damages represent a genuine pre-estimate of loss agreed upon by parties in advance.
Penalty is an extravagant or excessive amount fixed to compel performance or terrorize the party.
English law enforces liquidated damages but rejects penalties.
Indian law makes no distinction between liquidated damages and penalty under Section 74.
Courts in India award reasonable compensation not exceeding the sum named in the contract.
Exception: Breach of government bonds for public duty requires payment of the full sum specified.

flow.title: Treatment of Pre-fixed Damages under Indian Law
steps: Contract specifies fixed sum for breach
Breach of contract occurs
Court assesses actual loss suffered
Court awards reasonable compensation
Award sum cannot exceed stipulated amount

topics.example: A contract stipulates a penalty of Rs 1,00,000 for breach, but actual loss is Rs 70,000; court awards only Rs 70,000.
remember: In India, courts award reasonable compensation capped at the stipulated amount regardless of nomenclature.
mistakes: Assuming Indian courts enforce the exact penalty sum stated in a private agreement.

quiz.q: If a contract specifies Rs 50,000 penalty and actual loss is Rs 20,000, Indian courts will award:
quiz.why: Indian courts award reasonable compensation up to actual loss, capped at the stipulated sum.

quiz.q: Under English law, an excessive pre-fixed sum intended to threaten the defaulting party is called:
quiz.why: A penalty is an extravagant sum stipulated in terrorem of the offending party.

topics.title: Other Remedies for Breach of Contract
explain: Rescission cancels the contract, discharging the aggrieved party from future performance obligations.
Under Section 75, a party rightfully rescinding a contract can claim compensation for damage sustained.
Quantum Meruit means 'as much as earned', allowing payment for work already performed.
Quantum Meruit requires original contract discharge and can only be claimed by an innocent party.
Specific performance is ordered when monetary damages are inadequate, compelling exact performance.
Injunction is a court order restraining a party from doing an act promised not to do.

flow.title: Selecting Legal Remedies for Breach
steps: Breach of contract occurs by promisor
Cancel contract through rescission
Claim compensation under Section 75
Claim Quantum Meruit for work done
Request specific performance if damages inadequate
Seek injunction to prohibit negative acts

topics.example: Film star N agrees to act exclusively for producer P for one year but signs with another; court issues an injunction restraining N.
remember: Quantum Meruit is restitutory in nature and only available when the original contract is discharged.
mistakes: Believing Quantum Meruit can be claimed by a defaulting party who broke the contract.

quiz.why: Quantum Meruit means 'as much as earned' or deserved for work performed.

quiz.q: A court order prohibiting a person from doing a specific act promised not to be done is called:
quiz.why: An injunction is a court order restraining a party from carrying out a negative act.
